note: Agent Plasticity (arXiv 2610.08902v1, 2026-10-06). Headline numbers on screen: 298 (GPT-5.6 Sol estimated Psat), 57 (Claude Fable 5 estimated Psat) and 98% (GPT-5.6 Luna, share of relevant chess decisions without artifact use, pooled Hard and Easy chess). Psat is an estimated saturation-fit efficiency in score points per $1,000 of mean per-game learning cost on the combined chess, Go and Hex curve; it depends on the protocol and on provider pricing. All results are the authors' own runs.

numbers.298: GPT-5.6 Sol: estimated Psat 298 percentage points per $1,000 of mean per-game learning cost, combined chess, Go and Hex curve (sec 3.4, p. 7); an estimate from a saturation fit
numbers.57: Claude Fable 5: estimated Psat 57, same unit and curve (sec 3.4, p. 7); Claude Fable 5 also reaches the highest fitted performance level
numbers.98: GPT-5.6 Luna: about 98% of relevant decisions without artifact use, pooled Hard and Easy chess (sec 3.5, p. 8); labels from Gemini 3.1 Pro with execution evidence (sec 2.3, appendix G)
numbers.1,000: unit of the plasticity figures: score points per $1,000 of learning cost (sec 2.2, p. 4)
numbers.5: digit inside the model name Claude Fable 5 (bar tag)
numbers.2610.08902: arXiv id in the closing credit

claims.l01: Figure 8 and caption (p. 10): after dying at checkpoint 1 while praying through raw keystrokes, Claude Opus 5.5 adds a rule to pray only through its own controller; the game message is 'Killed by a dust vortex, while praying.' The rule was added to CLAUDE.md by the agent between checkpoints (sec 3.1, p. 6).
claims.l02: Sec 1 (p. 2) and sec 2.1 (p. 3): model weights remain frozen; each acting episode begins in a fresh context; future instances inherit tools, skills, strategies and textual memory (the artifacts).
claims.l03: Sec 2.2 (p. 4), verbatim: 'We operationalize agent plasticity as held-out performance gain per unit learning cost.' Receipt crop.
claims.l04: Sec 2.2 (p. 4): plasticity is reported in score points per $1,000 of learning cost; learning cost is token usage expressed in dollars as a proxy (sec 2.1). The plot is a schematic.
claims.l05: Abstract and sec 3.2 (p. 1 and 6): some models achieve substantial gains, others remain close to their initial performance, and a few decline.
claims.l06: Abstract (p. 1), verbatim: 'the agent that ultimately performs best need not be the one that improves most efficiently.' Receipt crop. Fable 5 has the highest fitted endpoint and Sol the highest estimated plasticity (sec 3.4, Finding 2). The curves are schematic.
claims.l07: Sec 3.4 (p. 7): on the combined three-game curve GPT-5.6 Sol has the highest estimated Psat at 298 percentage points per $1,000 of mean per-game learning cost, Claude Fable 5 has 57.
claims.l08: Sec 3.5 (p. 8): pooled over Hard and Easy chess, GPT-5.6 Luna takes about 98% of relevant decisions without artifact use. Relevant decisions are moves where at least one saved artifact is relevant (sec 2.3).
claims.l09: Sec 3.5 (p. 8): four lineages use artifacts at 94 to 98% of relevant chess decisions, and most of their remaining failures (83 to 99%) happen while a relevant artifact is in use. The tile grid is a schematic; the failure marks are illustrative and carry no share.
claims.l10: Sec 3.5 (p. 9), verbatim: 'Writing down an instruction is not the same as following it.' Receipt crop.
claims.l11: Sec 3.5 (p. 9): in one GPT-5.5 run the reflection step keeps telling the agent to load its saved move-picking program right away, yet the agent spends its first steps listing and reading files.
claims.l12: Sec 3.4 (p. 7): 'we interpret plasticity as a protocol-dependent measure, not a universal model ranking'; sec 4 (p. 10 to 11): estimates depend on score headroom, the learning horizon, saturation-fit assumptions and provider pricing.
claims.l13: Conclusion (p. 11): evaluating long-lived agents requires measuring not only what they can accomplish at a fixed point in time, but how their capabilities change through experience and how efficiently.
claims.l14: A question for the viewer; adds no claim. The hook words return as the answer.
